rynek: Main Market Square and St Mary's Basilica

One of Europe's largest medieval squares, with the Cloth Hall (Sukiennice) in the middle, the Town Hall Tower and St Mary's Church with its two different towers. Every hour a trumpeter plays the "hejnał" from the taller tower and breaks off abruptly mid-tune.
sukiennice: Cloth Hall: Gallery of 19th-Century Polish Art

The Renaissance market hall in the middle of the square: on the ground floor, stalls of amber, linen and souvenirs; upstairs, the National Museum gallery of 19th-century Polish painting, with Jan Matejko's huge historical canvases.
sotterr: Rynek Underground: the museum under the square
A museum below the square: you walk over the excavations of the medieval market, among reconstructed workshops, graves and screens telling the story of city life in the Middle Ages.
wawel: The hill on the Vistula with the castle of the Polish kings and the cathedral where kings and national heroes are buried. Inside are the royal apartments, the Crown Treasury, the tapestry halls and the Sigismund Bell. Below the hill is the dragon statue, linked to Kraków's most famous legend.
planty: Kraków's medieval walls: the Florian Gate with its tower, the round Barbican with its turrets and, all around the old town, the Planty ring park, which replaced the old moat. From the gate, Floriańska Street leads straight to the Rynek.
czart: Czartoryski Museum and the Lady with an Ermine

The museum holds Leonardo da Vinci's "Lady with an Ermine", his only painting in Poland, and Rembrandt's "Landscape with the Good Samaritan", along with arms, ceramics and objects collected by the Czartoryski princes.
kazimierz: Kraków's old Jewish quarter, now full of cafés, bars and murals. Around Szeroka Street are the Old Synagogue, one of Poland's oldest, housing the museum of Kraków's Jewish history, and the small cemetery next to the Remuh Synagogue. On Plac Nowy is the round hall selling "zapiekanki", toasted open baguettes.
schindler: Oskar Schindler's former enamel factory, now a museum about Kraków under Nazi occupation (1939–1945): life under occupation, the ghetto and the deportations, recreated with rooms, photos and witnesses' voices. It isn't the story of the film: it's a serious account of a city and its people, Jewish and Polish.
ghetto: Ghetto Heroes Square and the Eagle Pharmacy

The square that was the heart of the Jewish ghetto from 1941 to 1943. Today it's a memorial with dozens of large empty metal chairs, in memory of the deported residents. On one side is the Eagle Pharmacy, where the pharmacist Tadeusz Pankiewicz helped the ghetto's inhabitants.
